look_here_first: KLEBERG BLUESTEM (introduced): look for a many-fingered, often purplish silver terminal head AND a ring of relatively LONG WHITE HAIRS on true culm nodes; check often creeping/stoloniferous bases. But KR can have SHORT node hairs and silky bluestem also has a hairy ring. To separate confidently inspect a mature attached spikelet pair, awns and lower glumes; head count or hairs alone is not proof.

best_field_traits: FINGERED HEAD — multiple relatively slender terminal racemes, usually 2–9 in Flora of North America treatment; Texas A&M says 2–15. This OVERLAPS KR's 3–8+ terminal fingers.

TRUE NODE — often a conspicuous ring of long spreading white hairs at stem joints (not the blade collar); Texas material and global descriptions vary from glabrous to short-haired. Node alone is NOT species proof.
STOLONS — basal culms may lie on ground and root at nodes, especially in open/disturbed patches; KR may also spread under mowing, so habit alone is insufficient.

SPIKELET — sessile awned fertile spikelet plus pedicelled often staminate/sterile companion; mature awn often relatively long, twisted and bent, with a blunt to rounded lower glume and noticeable long hairs near glume upper margins.
LOWEST RACEME SPIKELETS — several basal pairs commonly sterile or male and awnless in Kleberg; document their positions on intact branches, not an isolated seedhead.
Conspicuous purplish or silver inflorescence colors overlap KR, silky bluestem and native Bothriochloa; never identify by color.
what_to_photograph_for_confirmation: Actual stem node WHITE ring hairs and creeping stolon/rootstock
One sessile awned vs one pedicelled companion spikelet at mm scale
Whole rooted clump with multiple culm nodes
crew_field_check: Start from whole rooted plant to establish growth form.
Photograph flowering head and collar on same individual.
Use hand-lens/25x macro to measure floret structure when needed; photos without it support only provisional source determination.
No county native certification; Kew states D. annulatum and D. sericeum are introduced in Texas.
morphology_keys.no_flower_safety: Find a true stem node and film/photograph spreading white hairs, then check the base for stolons and blade for papilla-based hairs near collar. KR may show short nodal pubescence and characteristic upper-blade papilla hairs; do not force an ID without a fertile head or voucher.
morphology_keys.spikelet_diagnostic: FNA: Kleberg sessile spikelets usually 2.5–5 mm with obtuse often 2–3-toothed lower-glume apex and cilia toward top, twisted twice-bent awn 13–22 mm; global floras extend this range. Pedicellate usually staminate. Compare in a measurable mature pair, because long awns or a single isolated glume are not wholly diagnostic.

comparisons.key_distinctions: KR vs Kleberg: both introduced grasses have clustered relatively long fingerlike racemes. Kleberg commonly has spreading LONG WHITE HAIR ring at true nodes and sometimes creeping rooted basal shoots; KR may have short/appressed nodal hairs plus distinctive stiff papilla-based hairs on UPPER blade just above collar. Kleberg lower glume often broadly obtuse with long upper marginal hairs; KR glume often more tapering, pedicellate spikelet generally hairless in local treatment. Compare mature attached spikelet pairs, glumes, pedicels and basal sterile pairs with 1-mm scale. D. sericeum ALSO has heavily hairy nodes; its typically sessile/subsessile densely silky racemes and specific glume marginal fringe require matched macro.

field_matrix.where_to_look: Compare the entire terminal panicle, two true stem nodes and upper blade surface at the collar on SAME rooted grass.
field_matrix.kleberg: Many slender fingers AND often a conspicuously SPREADING white hair ring at true stem nodes. Stolonlike lower stems common. Mature spikelet glume usually broad/obtuse with upper-marginal cilia.
field_matrix.look_alike: KR often has many terminal slender fingers too; node hairs absent or shorter/appressed in some sources; long stiff papilla-based hairs just above blade collar especially useful. KR often shows hairless sterile pedicelled spikelets in local UT account.
field_matrix.how_to_decide: A long white hair ring plus basal stolons supports Kleberg; papilla-based upper-blade hairs plus local mature spikelet shape favors KR. If only the flowering head is seen, label KR/Kleberg candidate — do NOT force species.

field_matrix.where_to_look: Use both species' licensed hairy-node photos: they SHARE obvious white hair rings.
field_matrix.kleberg: Commonly stalked subdigitate racemes, a variable count and basal unawned spikelet pairs; sessile lower glume broad and often hairy near apex.
field_matrix.look_alike: Silky often densely white-villous racemes, usually more nearly sessile/subsessile; lower glume with long subapical hair fringe in regional flora.
field_matrix.how_to_decide: Do not separate them by hairy nodes or silver color. Confirm intact rachis/stalk insertion and mature glume hair pattern under 10–20×.

field_matrix.where_to_look: Check true nodes and whole branching head, then inspect attached mature spikelets.
field_matrix.kleberg: Few-to-many slender terminal fingerlike racemes, true white nodal hair ring and often stolons.
field_matrix.look_alike: Cane has extremely prominent node beard plus broad fanlike panicle; silver forms a much narrower contracted cottony many-short-rame head.
field_matrix.how_to_decide: A hairy node may indicate native cane; protect uncertain specimens from invasive removal until the WHOLE flowering architecture is documented.

field_matrix.where_to_look: Trace each reproductive raceme to where it actually originates.
field_matrix.kleberg: Several longer fingers are clustered together in one terminal head.
field_matrix.look_alike: Many SHORT single fluffy racemes appear separately along upper leafy lateral shoots, with usually keeled basal sheath.
field_matrix.how_to_decide: Short separate flowering branches imply little bluestem; never remove a grass as Kleberg based on red or purple color alone.

not_reliable_alone: Silver-purple flowering head or number of fingers: overlaps KR and silky bluestem.
A white hair ring: also occurs in D. sericeum and can resemble native cane nodes.
Lack of conspicuous white node ring: North American Kleberg treatments may report smooth or only shortly hairy nodes.
Sprawling habit or stolons in mowed areas: KR can spread under repeated disturbance.
One detached spikelet photographed without pedicelled companion or base of raceme.

visual_comparison.title: KLEBERG vs KR — stem hair ring, terminal fingers and seed anatomy
visual_comparison.subtitle: One original archived Kleberg photo plus THREE visually checked, CC BY 2.0 external photographs from the same Macleay Grass Man source series. KR Texas terminal head and silky-bluestem hairy-node counterexample prevent false single-trait IDs.
visual_comparison.memory_rule: KLEBERG often has LONG SPREADING node beard + many fingers; KR often has PAPILLA hairs above leaf collar and sometimes short node hairs. Both have terminal fingers, and silky also has a node beard. Need attached mature glumes.

field_id_finish_pass.lookalikes: D. sericeum is an introduced silky bluestem also with very hairy silvery flowering branches, but often tufted with shorter rhizomes rather than distinctly stoloniferous. D. annulatum is strongly associated with unmistakable white-ringed stem nodes, and its full flowering head may bear more subdigitate racemes. Distinguish both from Bothriochloa/Schizachyrium with paired-spikelet + glume macro; photo of a red-purple foxtail alone is insufficient.

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: Kleberg vs KR — start on the real stem, then trace the fingers
steps: STEM NODE: white spreading hairs at the true joint on the blue-background picture. Do NOT mistake a leaf-blade collar for the joint.
FULL HEAD: trace the several upright racemes down to their junction. Similar KR head counts overlap, so use other characters.
AWN: trace the long bent lemma bristle back to a single fertile sessile spikelet. The sterile companion is NOT pictured.
COUNTERCHECK: open the Texas KR flowering head and the silky-bluestem node counterexample in the comparison gallery.
UNDECIDED? Keep KR/Kleberg sp. or introduced bluestem candidate until multiple characters on the same plant agree.
field_photo_quickcheck.field_rule: When both are introduced, the management group may be the same, but botany cards must not overclaim a species. Also rule out native cane/little/big/silver bluestems before removal.
field_photo_quickcheck.warning: These are licensed public photo references from Australian source plants, not independent Hays vouchers or same-plant photographs. Full local plant, paired mature spikelets and blade collar are still needed.

what_to_photograph_for_confirmation: Hays specimen rooted entire flowering culm and every terminal raceme attached.
Same true culm node with long spreading white hairs and ruler, and upper blade papilla hairs if present.
Same-plant basal stolon junction and rooted base.
Two to three mature spikelet pairs with fertile sessile, pedicellate partner, lower-glume obtuse apex and upper marginal hairs, 1-mm scale.
KR matched true node and upper collar with mature spikelet pair from verified Texas specimen.
Compare silky bluestem's equally hairy node with full flowering head, not detached macro alone.
